 ..... Respondents  JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against respondents, claiming compensation of Rs.13,060/- with respect to damages caused to the vehicle in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:
The petitioner is the owner of the Maruti Swift Dzire car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MF-4168 which was running by its owner on 12.05.2018 at 7.30 p.m. when it was going near palace of Sonnadenahalli Gate, Chintamani-Hosakote road, driving carefully on Sonnadenahalli Gate, Chintamani-Hosakote main road at Bengaluru, at that time, Zoom Car India Pvt. Ltd. Scorpio car bearing No.KA-03-AD- 7099 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed dashed against petitioner's car in its back side and on account of the same, the petitioner's car was pushed and dashed, due to which, petitioner's car sustained sever damages on its back side.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.13,060/- towards vehicle repair charges.
The accident was occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Scorpio Car.
The 1st respondent is the insurer, 2nd respondent is the driver and respondent No.3 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

3. The respondent No.4 has filed written statement and contended that the alleged accident was caused due to negligence of the petitioner himself as he drove his car rashly and negligently without maintain safe distance and lost the control over the vehicle and he himself has caused the accident.
On the date of the accident, the zoom car was being driven in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the zoom car.
The above petition is bad for non- joinder of necessary parties as the alleged accident was caused due to carelessness of the petitioner himself.

The above petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable as the insurer of the petitioner's car has considered the claim made by the petitioner towards damages caused to his car and settled the Own Damages Claim made by the petitioner as Full and Final Settlement and D.T. sentences.text: REASONS 9. ISSUE No.1 and 2:-

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the PW.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that the Maruti Swift Dzire car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MF-4168 which was running by its owner on 12.05.2018 at 7.30 p.m. driving carefully on Sonnadenahalli Gate, Chintamani-Hosakote main road at Bengaluru,
at that time, Zoom Car India Pvt. Ltd. Scorpio car bearing No.KA-03-AD-7099 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed dashed against petitioner's car in its back side and on account of the same, the petitioner's car was pushed and dashed, due to which, petitioner's car sustained sever damages on its back side.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.13,060/- towards vehicle repair charges.
The accident was occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Scorpio Car.
10. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the PW.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 4 which are the police records such as FIR, Complaint, Charge sheet and IMV report.

11. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri Suresh Babu D T, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.253/2018 of Hosakote Police Station for the offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279 of IPC.
12.

So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and the driver of the offending vehicle being cause for the accident is concerned, as per the case of the petitioner, petitioner being owner of the Maruti Swift Dzire car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MF-4168 running the said car at 7.30 p.m. near Sonnadenahalli Gate, Chintamani- Hosakote Main road driving carefully, at that time,
Zoom Car India Pvt. Ltd. Scorpio car bearing No.KA-03-AD-7099 came from his back side in a carelessly in a rash and negligent manner with high speed dashed against the petitioner's car from behind, on account of the same, petitioner's car pushed and dashed and petitioner's car sustained severe damages on its back side.

13. If the spot mahazar is perused, petitioner's car was going from Chintamani and the offending vehicle Scorpio car was also coming in the same direction from the back of the petitioner's vehicle and hit to the back portion of the petitioner's car and due to which, the petitioner's vehicle sustained damages.

The spot mahazar produced clearly shows that the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and due to his negligency, he has hit to the back side of the petitioner's vehicle and thereby caused damages to the vehicle.
Though respondent denied cause and manner of the accident, respondent has not led the evidence of the driver of the offending vehicle to disprove the testimony of the PW.1(petitioner).

The respondent No.4 denied the averments made in the petition and contended that the alleged accident was caused due to sole negligence of the petitioner himself and there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the Zoom car.
The IO under influence and without proper investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the Zoom car.

Even the investigating officer after thorough and detailed investigation have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P3 by D.T. Suresh Babu vs Ideal Insurance Brokers Pvt Ltd on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11410291/
4 holding that on 12.05.2018 at about 7.30 p.m. when petitioner was driving his car near Sonnadenahalli Gate, the driver of the offending vehicle drove his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and in the same direction and hit to the back of the petitioner's car and thereby caused the accident.

sentences.text: Though respondent examined the Investigating officer as RW.2, but not at all denied and disputed the charge sheet filed by the RW.2 and denied that the investigation conducted by him is false and defective.
No material and evidence are placed on record to prove that charge sheet filed by the investigating officer is defective and collusive.

Respondent except examined investigating officer,
has not examined the driver of the offending vehicle or any of the eye witnesses.

14. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
15. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

16. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of damage caused to his vehicle as the impact of the accident and the amount spent by him towards repair of the vehicle.

The petitioner has produced the Tax invoice bill and money receipt for the amount paid by him as per Ex.P6.

Further submitted that without prejudice to the above, respondent No.4 specifically submitted that this respondent has issued a policy of insurance in favor of 3rd respondent in respect of Zoom car and the liability of this respondent if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further submitted that 3rd respondent RC owner of the Zoom car has knowingly and willfully has entrusted the Zoom car to a person who did not had a valid and effective DL at the time of accident and there D.T. sentences.text: 19. With regard to the defence of respondent No.4 that as the insurer of the petitioner's car has considered the claim made by the petitioner towards damages caused to his car and settled the Own Damages Claim made by the petitioner as Full and Final Settlement and paid entire amount and hence the petition is not maintainable.

The petitioner in his petition at page No.6 clearly stated that after releasing car from the station and same was sent to the mechanics at Kalyani Motors private limited Bengaluru assessed repairs charges to set right the damage to petitioner's car at Rs.13,060/-
and the repair charges paid by him Rs.7,790/- was paid his car insurance company and the remaining amount of Rs.6,560/- was paid by the petitioner and hence respondent No.1 to 4 being the insurer, owner and driver of the Scorpio car bearing No.KA- 03-AD-7099 are jointly and severally liable make good of the said amount of Rs.13,060/- as compensation to the petitioner.
20.

Respondent No.4 examined the Legal Manager National Insurance company, insurer of petitioner vehicle as RW.1 who deposed that vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MF- 4168 has been insured with their company and they have considered the Own Damages Claim for Rs.7,790/- and as it was old case, the file has been destroyed.

Even though petitioner counsel cross examined RW.1 at length wherein RW.1 clearly stated that as on the date of accident, the policy was in force and denied the suggestion that their company has not paid Rs.7,700/- to the petitioner for repair charges.
RW.1 produced Ex.R3 OD Claim online payment approval advice which also shows that Insurance company of petitioner vehicle has paid Rs.7,700/- towards OD claim charges.s

Further in support of his contention, the petitioner has produced Ex.P6 Tax invoices of the Kalyani Motors Pvt.
Ltd., and receipt where he has got repaired his car which clearly shows that the repair charges of Rs.13,960/- and an amount of Rs.7,790/- paid by the National Insurance Company/respondent No.4.
Even petitioner himself has clearly admitted that he has received Rs.7,760/- from the respondent No.4 towards repair charges.

21. The learned counsel for respondent no.4 has vehemently submitted that since the petitioner has already received compensation of Rs.7,790/- under OD claim from his insurer towards full and final settlement of the claim, the claim made against the respondents is not maintainable.

22. The learned counsel for respondent No.4 relied upon the judgment reported in 2005 ACJ 1332 between Harkhu Bai & Ors., Vs. Jiyaram & Ors., wherein the Hon'ble High Court has observed that "when the payment was received by the claimant in full and final settlement of his claim without any reservation or demur, in the absence of any material to show that the claim paid by the other Insurance company represented a part only of the total damage, the rejection of the claim for any other payment is justified".
23.

It was held that claim to enforce subrogation rights is out side the jurisdiction of the claim tribunal.

24. In this regard, this Court further relied upon Judgment in MFA no. 5716 of 2010, between Ramesh Padiyar Vs. M N Laxminarayana Manja & Anr., on 15-02- 2019 decided by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, wherein also the petitioner got the compensation from his Insurance Company towards damages caused to his vehicle in full and final settlement.

entities.text: Ramesh Padiyar Vs. M N Laxminarayana Manja & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was observed that "Once the owner of the vehicle claimed compensation for the damages caused to the vehicle from its insurer and accepted the amount in full and final settlement of the claim, the owner of the said vehicle cannot claim compensation from the opposite vehicle Insurance Company and accordingly dismissed the petition".
25.

In MFA No. 4423/2013 between M/s MCCREADE SOFTWARE (ASIA) Rep., by its Managing Director Vs. Srinivas K & Ors., decided on 09-09-2015 wherein also the observation made in Harkhu Bai case was referred and observed that "when the claimant has got the loss suffered due to the damages caused in the accident assessed through its surveyor and loss assessor and received the OD claim of the petitioner in full and final settlement and when neither in the pleading nor in the evidence the claimant has made any effort to demonstrate that the amount received from its own insurer was not in full and final settlement and when the evidence of insurer is categorical to the effect that the payment made by the insurer is full and final settlement of the claim, the claim petition filed by the claimant is not maintainable, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed and accordingly dismissed the claim petition".
26.

In MFA No. 5788/2013 between Sri Kumarvel Janakiram Vs., The National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
& Ors., decided on 22-04-2024,

entities.text:
Sri Kumarvel Janakiram Vs., The National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
& Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the said case also by referring the judgment of Division Bench in Harkhu Bai case, it was observed that "since the claimant has received damages from his Insurance Company towards full and final settlement of claim without any reservation or demur, he is not entitled to claim compensation from the Insurer of offending vehicle by filing claim petition and accordingly claim petition filed by the petitioner against the Insurer of the offending vehicle was dismissed".
27.

Coming to the facts of the present case, if the evidence placed on record is perused, it is not in dispute that the petitioner has received compensation of Rs.7,790/- from the insurer of his vehicle towards Own Damage Claims.
If the evidence of the PW.1 coupled with the document Ex.P6 is perused, the amount charged for repair of the vehicle was Rs.13,960/-.
It is clear from the document that the insurer of the petitioner approved its liability to an extent of Rs.7,790/- and has paid Rs.7,790/- as full and final settlement.

When petitioner has received an amount of Rs.7,790/-
towards full and final settlement.

Under such circumstances, in view of discussions and observations made by the Hon'ble Courts in above said decisions, it can be said that petition is not maintainable against owner or insurer of offending vehicle that is all respondents.

Hence this Issue No.3 is answered as 'NEGATIVE'.
28. ISSUE No.4:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
Draw Award Accordingly.
